abstract: Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) XS is a low-latency, low-complexity wavelet codec that is promising for Internet Protocol (IP) transport of professional media both on-premises and in the cloud. A combination of standards and specifications, including SMPTE ST 2110-22, ISO/IEC 21122-3, Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) request for comments (RFC) 9134, and Video Services Forum (VSF) TR-08, define the transport of JPEG XS in realtime transport protocol (RTP) over IP. This article describes the essential details of that transport.

authors.bio: Thomas Edwards is a principal solutions architect at Amazon Web Services (AWS), Seattle, WA, USA, specializing in media and entertainment. Before joining AWS, he spent 20 years working for broadcasters Public Broadcasting Service (PBS), Fox, and Disney on satellite content distribution and digital TV projects, as well as exploring, proving out, evangelizing, and standardizing advanced media technology. He holds an MS in electrical engineering from the University of Maryland, College Park, MD. He is a SMPTE Fellow and was awarded the SMPTE Workflow Systems Medal for his work on live IP production technology.
